id: title:DanielVisca:add service metrics pivot to the span metrics tab

observations.behavior: Adds a ViewServiceMetricsButton component to render a link for viewing service-specific metrics.
observations.posthog_connection: Connects tracing spans with their associated service, allowing users to jump from an individual span view to broader service performance context.

observations.behavior: Changes date range calculation from useState to useMemo and keys it on span timestamp rather than just mount time.
observations.posthog_connection: Allows selecting different spans within the same drawer without resetting or refetching unrelated metric queries; preserves user intent when switching inspected spans.

observations.behavior: Tests that changing the selected span updates both the service name and the query window in the generated URL.
observations.posthog_connection: Confirms behavior change is working: clicking 'View metrics' now correctly targets the new span's service and its corresponding ±1 hour window.

observations.limitations: Only tests are shown. No implementation changes other than adding the button and wiring up the shared dateRange prop. The actual backend endpoint and permission checks are not demonstrated.

review.limitations: Only tests are shown. No implementation changes other than adding the button and wiring up the shared dateRange prop. The actual backend endpoint and permission checks are not demonstrated.
review.reason: This chunk demonstrates a bounded capability improvement: connecting existing trace inspection with warehouse/service-level metrics while preserving correct query windows across multiple selections. This could help PostHog users correlate distributed traces with underlying host workloads. However, no tier-3 systemic risk reduction or broad architectural change is demonstrated.
review.posthog_relevance: Adds value for debugging and diagnostics by bridging tracing and warehouse data, potentially reducing support effort and improving developer experience.
review.uncertainty: Assessment relies on test assertions rather than production implementation; adoption and benefit cannot be established from this chunk alone.
